about: The consecration of the chalice. Its words combine expressions from the institution narratives in Matthew 26, Mark 14, Luke 22 and 1 Corinthians 11. “Mystérium fídei” is not drawn from those accounts, while “ætérni” corresponds to Hebrews 13:20. The concluding command draws on Luke 22:19 and 1 Corinthians 11:25–26.

seg.tr: In like manner, after supper was ended,

fn.w001: “Símili modo” is an ablative of manner: “in a similar way”.
fn.w004: An impersonal past construction: “when supper was ended”.

seg.nr: The priest takes the chalice in both hands.

seg.tr: also taking this excellent chalice into His holy and venerable hands,

fn.w006: A present participle referring to Christ, the subject of “benedíxit” (w021).
fn.w009: The epithet with “Cálicem” (w010) — an echo of Ps 22:5: calix meus inébrians quam præclárus est.

seg.nr: The priest bows his head again.

fn.w017: An adverb marking the repetition of the bow made at the consecration of the bread.

seg.nr: Holding the chalice in his left hand, the priest makes the sign of the cross over it with his right.

seg.tr: He blessed it and gave it to His disciples, saying:

fn.w022: The narrative over the chalice has no “fregit”, which occurs with the bread.

seg.tr: Take and drink from it, all of you:

fn.w030: The pronoun refers to the chalice: “ex eo”, “from it”. With the bread the formula has “ex hoc”, “of this”.

seg.nr: The priest speaks the words of consecration over the chalice attentively, without break and silently, holding it slightly raised.

seg.tr: For this is the chalice of My Blood, of the new and eternal covenant: the mystery of faith: which will be shed for you and for many for the remission of sins.

fn.w038: A genitive agreeing with “testaménti” (w041), not with “Sánguinis” (w036).
fn.w040: This qualification does not occur in the institution narratives. “The blood of the eternal covenant” occurs in Hebrews 13:20.
fn.w041: A genitive depending on “Sánguinis” (w036) and modified by “novi” (w038) and “ætérni” (w040).
fn.w042: An independent nominative apposition to the words about the chalice of the Blood: Christ's Blood is present in the sacrament as a mystery held by faith.
fn.w044: “Calix” (w035) and “Sánguinis” (w036) are both masculine, so the pronoun's form does not resolve its antecedent. English likewise leaves it open.
fn.w050: Future, not past: at the moment of the Supper the blood had not yet been shed.

seg.nr: The words spoken, the priest sets the chalice on the corporal and says silently:

seg.tr: As often as you shall do these things, you shall do them in memory of Me.

fn.w056: A future perfect: an action complete before the one “faciétis” (w060) names. The same form can be a perfect subjunctive, and the future that follows decides it.
fn.w058: Genitive of the personal pronoun: “in memory of Me”.

seg.nr: The priest genuflects and adores, rises, shows the chalice to the people while the server rings the bell three times, sets it down, covers it and genuflects again.
